alias.description: A profile's handle (`ana`, or `ana@mastodon.social` for somebody on another server), or a hashtag's name.

name.description: A profile's name, or a post's title where it has one.

type.description: What kind of thing it is: `node.actor.<service>.person.v1`, `...group.v1`, `...event.v1`, or a post's kind.

Image.description: Image is one size of a picture.

ImageSize.description: ImageSize is how big an image is.

Item.description: Item is one rule, promise or suggestion: a short title, and a line more if it needs one.

offset.description: How many come before this page: what was asked for as `start`.

description.description: The same in words, for whoever is building a client.

error.description: Why, as a code a client can tell apart: `language_invalid`, `quote_not_allowed` and so on. Each route lists its own.

reason.description: What lies behind it, where one code has several causes: why a post may not be quoted, for one.

deleted_at.description: When it was deleted, while it waits out the thirty days before it is purged; absent otherwise.

email_verified.description: People only: whether they confirmed their address.

onboarded.description: People only: whether they went through the walk-through after signing up.

state.description: `active`, `disabled`, `archived` or `deleted` (on its way to being destroyed).

auth.PasskeyCount.description: PasskeyCount is how many passkeys somebody holds, and nothing else about them.

auth.PasskeysRevoked.description: PasskeysRevoked is how many passkeys were removed.

auth.PasswordChanged.description: PasswordChanged says how many other sessions were signed out.

revoked_sessions.description: Every one but the one that changed it.

auth.PersonTypeChanged.description: PersonTypeChanged is a person's type, and whether this changed it.

auth.SessionStarted.description: SessionStarted says the app's session holds its tokens now.

accepted_at.description: When. Null when they never have.

auth.nodeInfoServices.description: nodeInfoServices is what the installation bridges to and from: nothing.

inbound.description: Both are required by the schema and both are empty: this installation does not bridge to or from anything. They are `[]string{}` rather than nil because the schema says array, and a JSON null there makes strict consumers reject the whole document.

patch.description:
Registered, administrator or super administrator. An administrator may make somebody registered an administrator; making a super administrator, and taking a type away, are a super administrator's. Nobody changes their own, so the last super administrator cannot be demoted: one who wants to step down makes somebody else a super administrator first. Recorded with who did it (`made-registered`, `made-admin`, `made-super-admin`). It takes effect at the person's next token, within fifteen minutes.

Who may call it: a site administrator, with a token that carries `actors:write`, who has just proved who they are again.

404.description: `not_a_person`: no person here has that id; a group, a profile from another server and a deleted person have no type to change

parameters.description: RedirectURI uses the `uri` tag, not `url`. The `url` tag in go-playground/validator rejects any URI whose scheme isn't http/https — but RFC 8252 (OAuth 2.0 for Native Apps) explicitly recommends custom schemes for desktop and mobile apps because they route the callback to the registered app via the OS rather than through a browser. The `uri` tag accepts any valid URI with a scheme, which is the right syntactic check here.
